scope: Prospective routing-intent forwarding and per-firewall deny/permit differential, not a certificate of every native or final customer-wire AS string. Firewall allow/deny and SNAT are not simulator features; the deny matrix is an external causal traversal experiment.
inputPreconditions: Both hubs ExpressRoute preference; all common10.60/16 and specific10.60.1/24 auxiliary/VPN/MCR origins absent.
Unique ER inputs12076-12076, unique BGP VPN inputs65011/65012 and static VPN inputs empty; verify actual baseline before policy tests.
Spoke connections Internet security enabled before any intent. No Global Reach or support-enabled ER-to-ER firewall transit.
Two Standard secured-hub firewalls with private forwarding and scoped owned-VM control-plane/public HTTP access.
Public branch endpoint NSG permits8080 only from the two recorded owned firewall public IPs, above its existing Internet deny.
A top-priority firewall deny affects only the two owned workload source IPs, TCP8080 and the two exact owned probe destinations.
Synthetic ER common-prefix delivery, direct-spoke NVA as hub-integrated SDWAN, and exact final ER customer AS strings are excluded.
